# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-8 (Extended v85)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 2, approximately late 1825-1826)**: Valjean and Cosette in sanctuary at Convent of Petit-Picpus. Key dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont June 17-18); 1817 (young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest; Javert's revelation; TRIAL SEQUENCE in Arras; Valjean's self-revelation; acquittal of Champmathieu; RETURN TO M. SUR M. before six a.m.; Fantine's death; Valjean arrested beside death-bed; VALJEAN ESCAPES same evening)**; December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer Year 2**: Achieved sanctuary inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district. **Winter Year 2 (Current)**: A nun dying; community occupied with prayers of forty hours.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); **English harbor towns** (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Gulhaven); Arras; Waterloo; Toulon; Paris districts including Mouffetard quarter. **Gorbeau House** (Rue de la Cosette area, Mouffetard): Decrepit lodging where Valjean and Cosette previously lodged; old woman portress; Javert's surveillance station. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved roads. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above wall. **Wall (approximately 18 feet)**: Extends from niche to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur. **CONVENT COMPLEX - THREE BUILDINGS**: (1) **Great Convent**: Inhabited by Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy building, heavily shuttered window with sheet zinc. (2) **Boarding-school**: Where scholars lodged. (3) **Little Convent**: Building with garden housing aged nuns of various orders destroyed in Revolution. **INTERIOR GARDEN (Great Convent)**: Vast oblong area; alley of large poplars; forest trees in corners; solitary gnarled tree, fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass and green mould. **PARLOR (Great Convent)**: Monstrous lattice of iron bars (squares less than 1.5 inches diagonal) riveted by clenched-fist fastenings; behind lattice: barrier of black shutters reinforced with gingerbread-yellow wooden beams, always closed; behind shutters: nun's voice screened by iron grating and plate with thousand holes; slat opens revealing nun's mouth and chin only, covered with black veil, guimpe, shroud.

## Convent of the Bernardines of the Perpetual Adoration
**Order Lineage**: Bernardines-Benedictines of Martin Verga obedience; **1657 (Pope Alexander VII authorized Bernardines of Rue Petit-Picpus to practice Perpetual Adoration)**. **Dress**: Black clothing with white guimpe; serge robe with large sleeves; large woollen veil; novices wear all-white; professed nuns wear rosary at side. **Austerity**: Fast all year; abstain from meat; additional fasting in Lent; rise one to three a.m. for breviary and matins; sleep year-round on straw between serge sheets; never light fires; never bathe; scourge every Friday; strict silence except brief recreation; wear drugget chemises September 14 to Easter. **Vows**: Obedience, poverty, chastity, perseverance in seclusion. **Operational Rules**: Never see officiating priest (hidden behind nine-foot serge curtain); drop veils during sermons; speak low; walk with eyes down; only diocesan archbishop permitted entry; absolute passive submission to prioress (canonical subjection—at Christ's voice, at gesture, at first sign, immediately with cheerfulness, perseverance, blind obedience); cannot read or write without express permission. **Reparation Practice**: Each nun in turn performs twelve-hour continuous reparation prayer on knees on stone before Holy Sacrament, hands clasped, rope around neck; when fatigue unbearable, prostrates flat against earth, arms outstretched as cross. **Possessions Rule**: Never say "my"; call everything "our". **Hourly Bells**: At each hour three supplementary church bell strokes; all interrupt activity and say formula praising Most Holy Sacrament. **Chanting**: Solemn psalmody, pure Gregorian chant; for office of dead adopt tone so low women's voices can barely descend. **Burial Issue**: Vault beneath grand altar for community burials; Government forbids coffin burial in vault, so nuns leave convent when die. **Convent Communication System—Bell-Telegraph Network**: Rule of silence withdrew speech from human creatures; speech bestowed on inanimate objects—church-bell and gardener's bell. Each person and thing had own peal: prioress one-and-one; sub-prioress one-and-two; six-five announced lessons; four-four was Madame de Genlis's signal. **Nine strokes announced great event: opening of door of seclusion**. **Men Allowed in Convent (Three Only)**: Archbishop, chaplain Abbé Banés, drawing-master M. Ansiaux/Anciot.

## Prioress and Vocal Mothers (1819-1825 Period)
**Mademoiselle de Blemeur (Mother Innocente)** (Prioress, 1819-1825): Age ~sixty; short, thick; "singing like a cracked pot"; excellent woman; only merry one in convent; learned, erudite, wise; proficient in history; descended from Marguerite de Blemeur, author of _Lives of the Saints of the Order of Saint-Benoît_; re-elected. **Vocal Mothers**: Mother Sainte-Honorine; Mother Sainte-Gertrude (treasurer); Mother-Saint-Ange; Mother Annonciation (sacristan); Mother Saint-Augustin (nurse; only malicious one); Mother Sainte-Mechtilde (directs singing); Mother des Anges; Mother Saint-Joseph; Mother Sainte-Adélaide; Mother Miséricorde; Mother Compassion; Mother Providence; Mother Présentation (future prioress 1847); Mother Sainte-Céligne; Mother Sainte-Chantal. **Order Decline**: Forty years before 1845, nuns numbered nearly a hundred; by 1845, none professed nuns, only lay-sisters.

## Resident Women in Little Convent
**Madame Albertine**: Woman not a nun, ~thirty years old; dark complexion; tolerably pretty; passed for dead in world; possessed strange spectral grace. **Other Resident Women**: Madame Beaufort d'Hautpoul, Marquise Dufresne. **Centenarian from Abbey of Fontevrault**: Talked of eighteenth century. **Nun of Sainte-Aure**: Only survivor of her order; **1824: only doll remains**.

## Jean Valjean's Sanctuary and Strategic Position
**ESCAPE FROM M. SUR M.** (January 1823 evening): Successfully fled jail after Javert's arrest beside Fantine's death-bed; climbed 18-foot wall; placed Cosette on back; descended safely to interior garden via roof. **REFUGE DISCOVERY AND FAUCHELEVENT**: Encountered elderly crippled gardener Fauchelevent, admitted to convent approximately two years previously (1821) on Mayor Madeleine's recommendation after falling from cart. **COSETTE**: Now sleeping in Fauchelevent's bed; rosy; completely dependent on Valjean. **CURRENT LOCATION** (Winter Year 2): Still secured in convent sanctuary. **VALJEAN'S UNDERSTANDING OF DANGER AND SAFETY**: Upon realization Javert pursued him and Cosette from Gorbeau house, understood they were lost if returned to Paris. Convent represents paradox: **most dangerous place** (flagrant offence if male discovered; step between convent and prison) and **safest place** (impossible location where no one would seek him; if accepted as resident, absolute sanctuary). Strategic necessity: remain in convent. **PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE**: Altered appearance reflects sadness, uneasiness, anxiety, depression; continual tremor so long as Cosette near, needs nothing except her, fears nothing except her.

## Fauchelevent's Role and Commitment
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener; admitted approximately two years previously on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. **Character**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; speaks freely; peasant of Picardy; old egoist who toward end of days found sweetness in gratitude. **Current Occupation**: Spreading straw mats over melon beds in garden; wears bell and kneecap device. **Hospitality**: Provided Cosette safe bed; offered cheese, black bread, wine. **Commitment to Valjean**: Perceived generous action (keeping Valjean and Cosette in convent) as dying man perceives glass of good wine—grasped with avidity. **Air of Convent Effect**: Long residence in convent destroyed all personal selfishness, rendered good action absolutely necessary to him. **Current Plan**: Undertook to scale difficulties of cloister and steep escarpments of Rule of Saint-Benoît; enlisted self-devotion, good will, and old rustic cunning in generous enterprise. **Status**: Valjean's only known ally and protector in Paris; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's presence. **Opportunity**: One of the nuns currently dying; community occupied with prayers of forty hours; this confusion prevents close observation. **Caution**: Will not answer for tomorrow.

## Javert's Pursuit and Ongoing Investigation
**REASSIGNMENT TO PARIS** (January 1823): When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail, Javert attached to Paris police force. **NEWSPAPER REPORT** (December 1823): Newspaper announced Valjean's death; Javert read, remarked "That's a good entry." **REACTIVATION**: Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived Javert's memory; suspected Valjean had sought daughter. **JAVERT'S SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence. **REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead was magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen—preferred elaborating masterpieces in dark. **PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; at night Javert waited behind trees with two men. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder in lantern, led astray toward Cul-de-Sac Genrot. **STRATEGIC PURSUIT**: Followed Valjean from tree to tree; why not arrested?—considered abrupt demand for papers risky; to arrest hastily would "kill the hen that laid golden eggs." Allowed man to go ahead, gloating with voluptuousness of spider allowing fly to flutter. **MOMENT OF LOSS**: Even when saw Valjean escaped, did not lose head; sure convict could not be far off, established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades. **Impediment to Arrest**: Free press embarrassed police; arbitrary arrests denounced by newspapers; police agents afraid of mistakes.

## English Harbor Towns Communities
**Recurring Named Residents**: Matho Stenson, Ismira Stenson, Pelde Stenson, Harine Lindmere, Davus Stenworth, Havus Stenworth, Volia Brackick, Nelan Brackick, Kadrek Brackick, Rinelle Corrley, Lurald Stenworth, Volan Stenworth, Luwyn Brackick, Rovus Prydenridge, Gadrek Prydenridge, Ludrek Prydenridge, Movie Prydenridge, Isric, Islan Thornmere, Malis Prydenridge, Havie, Vesmira, Wenelle Lindmere, Nerine Prydenridge (newborn daughter of Wenelle and Rovus, born in Ostcombe), Luvie, Jotho. **Towns/Locations**: Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Gulhaven, Ostcombe, Kelmere pastures. **Key Fact**: Lurald Stenworth revealed deed to Kelmere pastures was forged; letter burned by Nelan Brackick. **Recent Events**: Malis Prydenridge died of long wasting sickness, laid in churchyard at Ostcombe; Luwyn Brackick and husband moved from Kelford to Dunstead after quarrel; salt prices discussed as scandal. **Recurring Activities and Atmosphere**: Reading almanacs; sorting letters; discussing weather, harvest, lame horse, salt prices; aching backs; baker's boy late; rain threatening; bees humming in lavender; frost silvering hedges; wind from water with salt and tar smell; children chasing hoop down lane, shrieking; carts with turnips; coin counting; light going early in year.

## Narrative Commentary (Author's Philosophical Perspective)
**On Philosophy's Function**: Philosophy should be energy ameliorating human condition; man of wisdom should emerge from man of felicity; science should be cordial; ideal should be practicable, breathable, drinkable, eatable to human mind; wisdom is holy communion, becomes sovereign mode of human rallying, promoting philosophy herself to religion. **On Monasticism and the Ascetic**: Ascetic and sage converge in mingling with life presence of the sepulchre; there is material growth and moral grandeur. Whoever exiles himself in this age seems worthy of veneration when so many mortals' morality consists in enjoyment and brief misshapen things of matter. Monastery, particularly female convent, has incontestable majesty; in current century woman suffers most, and cloister exile contains something of protestation. Yet **cloistered existence is not life (lacks liberty) nor tomb (lacks plenitude)**—strange place from crest of lofty mountain viewing abysses on both sides; narrow misty frontier separating two worlds, illuminated and obscured simultaneously; half obscurity of tomb. **On Respect for the Devoted**: Those who live by faith, though not believing what nuns believe, regard devoted, trembling, trusting creatures with tender religious terror and pitying envy; these humble, august souls dare dwell on brink of mystery, waiting between closed world and unopened heaven, eyes fixed motionless on darkness, kneeling, bewildered, stupefied, shuddering, half lifted by deep breaths of eternity.
